vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
A **technical SEO or AI-search (GEO) specialist** can check the blocks and make the changes. Ask for a technical audit—not just a promise to “get you into ChatGPT.”

For example, **Levy Online** specifically describes checking AI crawler access and configuring `robots.txt`; **Thrive** and **WebFX** offer broader AI-search audits that include technical SEO. These are starting points, not endorsements.  
- [Levy Online](https://www.levyonline.com/services/ai-seo/chatgpt-seo/)  
- [Thrive Agency](https://thriveagency.com/digital-marketing-services/ai-seo-services/)  
- [WebFX](https://www.webfx.com/seo/services/ai-search-optimization/)

Ask them to verify which AI bots are blocked, check `robots.txt` and any CDN/firewall rules, and confirm your important pages are crawlable and readable. For ChatGPT search visibility, **OAI-SearchBot** is especially relevant; allowing **GPTBot** is a separate choice related to model training. You can allow search access without necessarily allowing training use.

You could also start by asking your web developer or hosting provider to check the settings. Don’t hand over passwords; have them explain each proposed change and whether it affects your privacy or security. Opening access makes your site eligible to be read—it **doesn’t guarantee** that an AI assistant will mention or recommend your business.
